origin.basis: Schwalbe is the brand of Ralf Bohle GmbH, Reichshof, Germany (legal notice).

manufacturing.basis: The Schwalbe product pages do not state where the tire is made.

availability.note: Schwalbe's European and North American sites give recommended retail prices and send buyers to retailers; mainland China availability not verified.

name: One (tube type)
positioning: Schwalbe's all-round tube-type road tire with an ADDIX compound and RaceGuard belt.
caveats: Needs an inner tube; the One Tubeless is listed separately.
No independent lab test of this version recorded.

price_observations.conditions: Recommended retail price on the official product page on 2026-11-01; one tire; retailer prices vary.

owner_evidence.screening_note: Coded on 2026-11-04 from a fixed source set: the written reviews on the Sigma Sports and bike-components product pages, read in full through each page's own review list (the newest 15 per page when more exist), every reader comment on Bicycle Rolling Resistance's test pages for this tire, and owner comments in coded Xiaohongshu threads. Counted only owners who describe their own riding; star-only ratings, reviews without riding detail, mounting-only impressions and repeats were left out. Comments on one construction's test page count for that construction unless the owner names the other. Colour options and the E-25-rated listing count as the same tire; reviews of the earlier One V-Guard are not counted.

reports.summary: Running well on a winter bike, with plenty of grip on rough roads.
Low rolling resistance, good grip and fairly puncture-resistant for a summer tire, lasting about 2,000-3,000 km.
Good grip and satisfying, but worn to the casing at 3,000 km.
A good balance of speed and durability in 30 mm: fast, and ridden for a long time in training, racing and winter grit without damage.
A good product despite a first puncture after 800 km.
Light and comfortable, with excellent puncture protection even on gravel and confident cornering grip; still like new after more than a year and a few thousand kilometres.
Runs true and mounts easily; comfortable and fast enough, though narrower than the old One Evo.
Much more comfortable than the Continental tire it replaced on a gravel bike, and still fast.
A robust, easy-rolling tire, though up to 20 g over the claimed weight.
The owner says it covers a lot of kilometres.

checks.note: Two listings; one review reports only a delivery error
